offerText: Your first article is on me.

signal.text: RPR ranks #1 for 'augmented reality in events', but Google's AI Overview above it cites Onirix.

cards.title: WebAR After 8th Wall: Buyer's Guide
cards.angle: 8th Wall's hosted platform ended February 28, 2026. Every guide to what comes next is written by a platform selling itself. RPR can write the neutral one.
cards.evidence: Search '8th Wall alternatives' and every result is a vendor: Zapworks, Kivicube, Blippar, Arloopa. The engine is now MIT open source without SLAM, VPS, Maps, or hand tracking. Your 'Is WebAR Better than AR Apps?' page predates all of it and folds into this pillar.

cards.title: Google Maps AR for Brands
cards.angle: Location-based AR inside Google Maps needs no app and no QR code. RPR shipped the first-of-its-kind launch and has the award to prove it.
cards.evidence: Your Paris landmarks launch with Google Arts and Culture was covered by Forbes, and won the 2025 Auggie Award for AR in Google Maps. No page on your site explains how a brand buys it.

sources.title: Google Maps introduces AR for Paris landmarks with Rock Paper Reality
First-of-its-kind AR content launch in Google Maps

cards.title: AR Glasses for Brands: What to Build
cards.angle: The first glasses wave is audio, not holograms. Android XR launches audio glasses this fall and display glasses have no date. Brands should build for voice and navigation now, and for visual AR on Snap's Specs.
cards.evidence: Google confirms Android XR audio glasses with Gentle Monster and Warby Parker this fall. Display glasses are listed as 'stay tuned'. Snap's display Specs are reportedly priced at $2,500. Navigation is a launch feature, which is where your Google Maps work lands. Your Vision Pro piece is written for a headset moment that has passed.

sources.title: Snap's AR glasses with display reportedly beat Android XR to launch

cards.title: AR for Events: Win the AI Overview
cards.angle: RPR is the #1 result for 'augmented reality in events', yet Google's AI Overview above it quotes Onirix. Restructure the page so the answer engine quotes RPR.
cards.evidence: Google search, September 24, 2026: your page is the first organic result, directly beneath an AI Overview citing Onirix and a LinkedIn post.

sources.title: Google search: augmented reality in events (Sep 24, 2026)

cards.title: VR in Museums: Cost and Timeline
cards.angle: You rank top 3 for what VR does in museums. The next thing a museum director searches is what it costs, and nobody answers it.
cards.evidence: Google search, September 24, 2026: 'How Virtual Reality is Transforming Museums' ranks top 3. Cost searches return museums' own ticketed VR attractions, not a buyer's guide.

sources.title: Google search: virtual reality in museums (Sep 24, 2026)

cards.title: Replacing 8th Wall VPS With Google Geospatial
cards.angle: 8th Wall's VPS is gone. For location-anchored campaigns, Google's Geospatial stack is the replacement, and RPR has already shipped on it.
cards.evidence: Links your two pillars: the 8th Wall buyer's guide and Google Maps AR for Brands. Built on your Google Maps launch.

sources.title: Geospatial Creator: world-scale AR in minutes
First-of-its-kind AR content launch in Google Maps

cards.title: AI in XR Production: Where Budget Moved
cards.angle: Generative AI didn't make immersive cheaper. It moved budget from building assets to designing the experience.
cards.evidence: Builds on Preston Platt's AWE USA 2025 session, which lives on your Insights page only as an event recap.

sources.title: Insights (AWE USA 2025: How AI Supercharged XR)

cards.title: Experiential AR ROI: What to Measure
cards.angle: Events buyers ask what an activation returned. Give them the four numbers that answer it, and the one that doesn't.
cards.evidence: The follow-up to your #1 events page. Extends Omead Sinai's AWE USA 2025 talk on why events matter more than ever.

sources.title: Insights (AWE USA 2025: Why Events Matter More Than Ever)

cards.title: Gaussian Splatting for Museum Tours
cards.angle: Splats capture a gallery in an afternoon at photographic realism. For museums and attractions, that changes what a virtual tour costs.
cards.evidence: Pairs your existing Gaussian Splatting article with the museum buyers you already rank for. Leaves the original article untouched.

sources.title: Gaussian Splatting: When Does it Make Sense to Use and Why?

cards.title: Location-Based AR for Tourism Boards
cards.angle: Tourism boards want visitors to stay longer at a site. Location AR in Maps puts the story on the landmark itself, with no app to download.
cards.evidence: Connects your tourism use-case page to the Google Maps pillar and the Paris landmarks launch.

sources.title: First-of-its-kind AR content launch in Google Maps
